title: fix(plugin-view,app-shell): refresh the view in place after a write instead of remounting it (objectui#10035)
body:
Part of #10035
Clause-②: no

## What this changes

AGENTS.md commandment 8's corollary: refresh data, don't rebuild UI. Both `ObjectView` layers carried their refresh counter in a React `key`, so every write remounted the view. This PR takes the counter out of the key wherever the rendered view can refetch in place, and hands it over as a data signal instead:

- `@object-ui/app-shell` `renderListView`: `ListView` is keyed on object + view id only (`identityKey`), and the combined counter (page counter + plugin ObjectView counter) now reaches it as `refreshTrigger`, which `ListView`'s fetch effect already lists. Before this, the page's own counter (record actions, import, realtime, view edits, the console's `externalRefreshKey`) reached `ListView` through the key alone, so dropping the key without the relay would have silently lost those refetches.
- `@object-ui/plugin-view` `renderContent`: the non-grid branch keys kanban / calendar / gallery / timeline / map / tree on the view identity only; they draw the rows the non-grid fetch effect re-reads when `refreshKey` moves.

⚠️ Partial on purpose, hence `Part of`: three renderers have **no in-place refetch path**, so they keep the counter in their key, each set named and commented (`REMOUNT_TO_REFRESH_VIEW_TYPES` in plugin-view, `REMOUNT_TO_REFRESH_VISUALIZATIONS` in app-shell). Fixing them needs a child edit outside this claim's file surface (see "The half that stays" below).

## Measurement: what refetches each view after a write, once the key stops moving (dispatch assumption A1)

Read on `origin/main` `cff4b7754`.

| site / branch | renderer | in-place refetch path | key after this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| plugin-view, `renderListView` branch | host list view | the key was never applied there; host receives `refreshKey` and `schema.refreshTrigger` | unchanged |
| plugin-view, kanban | `ObjectKanban` | draws host `data` (fetch effect names `refreshKey`); with external data it does not subscribe itself ("Parent handles refresh") | identity |
| plugin-view, calendar | `ObjectCalendar` | same external-data path | identity |
| plugin-view, gallery / timeline / map | `ObjectGallery` / `ObjectTimeline` / `ObjectMap` | draw `props.data`; map's effect names `dataProp` | identity |
| plugin-view, tree (host-only type) | `ObjectTree` | queries for itself, but its fetch effect names the host `data`, so a new array re-issues its query | identity |
| plugin-view, gantt | `ObjectGantt` | **none**: the registered `object-gantt` renderer hands it only `schema` and `dataSource`; its `reload` effect names no counter, no `onMutation`, no invalidation bus | identity + counter (kept) |
| plugin-view, chart (host-only type) | `ObjectChart` | **none**: own aggregate query off the node; reads neither host `data` nor a refresh input | identity + counter (kept) |
| plugin-view, grid (and unknown types) | `ObjectGrid` | **none from the host**: its query moves only on its internal counter (pull-to-refresh, its own row/bulk actions, inline save); no `onMutation`, no refresh prop | identity + counter (kept) |
| app-shell, view type `chart` | `ObjectChart` in `Suspense` | **none** (as above) | identity + counter (kept; same string as before) |
| app-shell, `ListView` for grid / kanban / calendar / gallery / timeline / map / tree | `ListView` | `refreshTrigger` (now the combined counter) + its own `onMutation` subscription; children draw `ListView`'s rows, tree re-queries on them | identity |
| app-shell, `ListView` that can draw gantt or chart (its own `viewType`, or the author's `appearance.allowedVisualizations` through the in-list switcher) | `ObjectGantt` / `ObjectChart` | **none**; and this host cannot see which visualization the switcher shows | identity + counter (kept) |

A2 held: object, view id and view type stay in the key, so switching view / object / type is still a remount (the objectui#10046 view-switch control stays green).

A3, measured: neither `notifyDataChanged` nor its reader hook reaches any of these renderers. The bus readers (`useDataInvalidation`) are app-shell's record detail, related-record actions and signed-in-user locale hook, `plugin-detail`, and plugin-grid's per-record CRUD-verdict hook (a permission answer, not the grid's rows); `ListView`, `ObjectGrid`, `ObjectKanban`, `ObjectCalendar`, `ObjectGantt`, `ObjectChart`, `ObjectGallery`, `ObjectTimeline`, `ObjectMap` and `ObjectTree` do not subscribe. (`useDataRefresh`, the name in the dispatch, exists in `@object-ui/react` with zero `src` consumers.) So the smallest change is to keep `refreshKey` as the signal and relay it through `refreshTrigger`, the input `ListView` already reads — the same channel the Studio Data pillar's `renderStudioGridList` relies on.

A5: no existing test asserted remount-on-refresh. One docstring sentence in `ObjectView.refreshSignal.test.tsx` said the counter is read "by the child-view remount key"; it now says the remount key of the views that cannot refetch in place.

## Tests

New pins, one file per site:

- `packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.refreshInPlace-10035.test.tsx` — a data-fed view (kanban, calendar, gallery, timeline, map, tree) keeps its instance across an `onMutation` write (a) and receives the refetched rows (b); gantt, chart and grid still get a fresh instance.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.refreshInPlace-10035.test.tsx` — the real page, plugin ObjectView and `ListView`; an `externalRefreshKey` bump (what the console sends after a record-form save, undo, redo) re-issues the list query exactly once (b) while a node read inside `ListView` is the same node afterwards (a); a list whose type is gantt, or whose whitelist offers gantt, still remounts.

Reverse run and ablations, every leg restored through a trap / `ablation-replace` wrap and proven by blob hash == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`, at `42737c855`:

| leg | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| R | both source files back to `cff4b7754` | 8 red / 5 green: every in-place case red on (a) (instance 2 where 1; list node replaced), with (b) passing first — the pre-fix world refetched too, through the remount; the 5 kept-remount cases green |
| A1 | app-shell `refreshTrigger: combinedRefreshKey` deleted | 2 red / 2 green: both app-shell in-place cases red on (b) — the list never re-queried |
| A2 | plugin-view non-grid fetch effect stops naming `refreshKey` | 6 red / 3 green: every in-place case red on (b) (`find` called once, expected twice). ⚠️ The first A2 attempt was a no-op: its replacement text already occurred inside the anchor, and `ablation-replace` refused it (replacement count rose by 0); rerun with a distinct replacement |
| A3 | app-shell whitelist dropped from the reachable-visualization list | 1 red / 3 green: the whitelist case red |
| A4 | both remount sets emptied | 4 red / 9 green: plugin-view gantt + chart and both app-shell kept-remount cases red; grid keeps its own key |

## Gates (all at `42737c855`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-view/` — 46 files / 428 tests passed.
- Every app-shell test file that mentions `ObjectView`, the new pin among them — 67 files / 698 tests passed (two runs: 52 + 15).
- Closure build `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'` (28 tasks) exit 0, then `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exit 0 for `@object-ui/plugin-view` and `@object-ui/app-shell`.
- ESLint on the 5 touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files, `--format json`: 5 files, 0 errors. Warnings sit on untouched lines of the two source files, plus `no-explicit-any` in the new tests (same as the sibling refresh test). Why this narrowing is complete: `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService` and no custom rule in `eslint-rules/` reads the disk, so a file's result depends only on its own text and the config, and this diff changes neither for any untouched file.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:changeset-claims` (5 pending bodies name a touched file; each paragraph re-read, none is about keys or refresh, all still true), `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:self-import`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unreferenced-sources` — all exit 0. `check-governed-queue-guard --test`: NOT GOVERNED.

## The half that stays (why this is `Part of`)

`ObjectGrid` (plugin-grid), `ObjectGantt` (plugin-gantt) and `ObjectChart` (plugin-charts) read no refresh input, so a host can only show them a write by remounting them. The same gap exists inside `ListView`: its own toolbar Refresh and its `onMutation` refetch never reach a gantt or chart visualization, because those query for themselves. Closing it means a child edit (for example, each of the three following `useDataInvalidation` or a host refresh counter), which is outside this claim's surface; the report names it for the seat.

## Acceptance notes

- Kept remounts are named sets with a "do not drop a member" comment, and the kept-remount cases pin them: removing a member without a renderer change goes red by name (leg A4).
- A list that whitelists gantt or chart remounts for every visualization, not only while the switcher shows gantt/chart — this host cannot see the switcher's state. Conservative on purpose: the alternative is a gantt that silently stops showing writes.
- `ListView` may now fetch twice after a write through the data source (its `onMutation` handler plus `refreshTrigger`); its own comment already records that `find()` coalesces concurrent identical reads.
